title: Withdrawing an Appeals and Grievances Case: Member Conditions
content:
A member may withdraw an **Appeals and Grievances** case on the following conditions.

## Conditions

1. The member may withdraw a case orally or in writing at any time before resolution, and may file again while the original filing deadline still runs.
2. A withdrawn case ends any continuation of services the next day.

## What withdrawal means on the case

- A case can be withdrawn from filed, acknowledged or under review status; a resolved case is no longer open to withdrawal.
- The withdrawal is made by the member. The case then shows the status withdrawn, the outcome withdrawn, and the date of withdrawal as its closing date.
- Whether withdrawal by phone and filing again are open is set per case type; both are open on every case type.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- **Timing of the end of continuation.** A Standard Appeal with services continuing is withdrawn on 10 April. The continuation of services ends on 11 April, the next day.
- **Filing again.** A member's adverse benefit determination notice is dated 1 March, and the case type's filing deadline is taken as 60 calendar days, so the original deadline runs through 30 April. The member withdraws the appeal on 20 March. A new filing on 15 April falls while the original deadline still runs; a new filing on 2 May falls after it and outside what this condition allows.
- **A resolved case.** A case already resolved cannot be withdrawn, since withdrawal is available only before resolution.
